key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating properties depend on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF yields a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and spray process can help tailor protective coatings for machine parts exposed to intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compare detonation-sprayed and HVOF-deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examine powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test conditions, variability, or comparative wear rates, limiting assessment of service-life gains.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
